units.source_text: 这是没有月亮的时候，侍女们点起灯笼来。

en.t: It was a moonless time, and the ladies-in-waiting lit the lanterns.

units.source_text: 源氏说：“靠近灯笼，毕竟太热，还不如点篝火的好。”

en.t: Genji said, "It is too hot near the lanterns after all; a brazier fire would be better."

units.source_text: 便召唤侍女，吩咐她们：“拿一台篝火到这里来。”

en.t: He then called the attendants and ordered them, "Bring a brazier fire here."

units.source_text: 这里放着一张优美的和琴，源氏取过来弹一下，弦音十分协律，音色亦甚良好，便弹了一会。

en.t: A fine wagon lay there, and Genji took it up and tried it; the strings were beautifully tuned and the tone was excellent, so he played for a while.

units.source_text: 对玉鬘说：“你不大喜欢音乐么？

en.t: He said to Tamakazura, "Are you not very fond of music?

units.source_text: 我见你一向不重视它。

en.t: It has always seemed to me that you do not value it much.

units.source_text: 凉月当空的秋夜，坐在稍稍靠近窗前的地方，合着虫声而弹奏和琴，其音亲切而新颖，非常可爱呢。

en.t: On an autumn night with a cool moon overhead, sitting a little near the window and playing the wagon in harmony with the insects' voices gives a sound that is intimate, fresh, and very charming.

units.source_text: 和琴虽然规模不大，构造简单，然而这乐器具备其他许多乐器的音色与调子，确有其独得的长处。

en.t: Though the wagon is not large and is simply made, it contains the tones and modes of many other instruments, and truly has virtues all its own.

units.source_text: 世人称之为和琴，视为甚不足道之物，其实具有无限深幽之趣。

en.t: People call it the wagon and treat it as something of little account, but in truth it has an endlessly deep and subtle charm.

units.source_text: 我想，这乐器大约是为了不习种种外国乐器的女子而制造的吧。

en.t: I think this instrument was probably made for women who do not study the various foreign instruments.

units.source_text: 你如果要学音乐，最好专心学习和琴，合着其他乐器而练习弹奏。

en.t: If you wish to learn music, it would be best to devote yourself to the wagon and practice playing it together with other instruments.

units.source_text: 其弹奏技法，虽然并无多少深奥秘诀，但真要弹得好，也不是一件容易的事。

en.t: Its technique may not contain many profound secrets, but to play it truly well is not an easy thing.

units.source_text: 在当代，无人比得上这位内大臣。

en.t: In our time, no one can equal this Minister of the Center.

units.source_text: 同是简单平凡的清弹，手法高明之人弹来，含有各种乐器的音色，其声美不可言。”

en.t: Even the same simple, plain solo playing, when performed by someone of great skill, contains the tones of many instruments, and the beauty of its sound is beyond words."

units.source_text: 玉鬘也曾约略学过和琴，如今听了源氏之言，颇思再图上进，学习之心更切了，便问：“这院内举行管弦之会时，我也可以去听听么？

en.t: Tamakazura too had once learned a little wagon, and now, hearing Genji's words, she felt a strong wish to improve and became even more eager to study, so she asked, "When musical gatherings are held in this mansion, may I go and listen too?

units.source_text: 山野愚民之中，学和琴的人也很多，人皆以为这乐器很简单，容易学会。

en.t: Even among simple folk in the hills and fields, many people learn the wagon, and everyone thinks the instrument is simple and easy to master.

units.source_text: 原来名手弹奏时，如此高深美妙。”

en.t: Yet when a master plays it, it is so profound and beautiful."

units.source_text: 她那态度非常热情，表示十分羡慕的样子。

en.t: Her manner was very earnest and showed how deeply she admired it.

units.source_text: 源氏说：“这个自然。

en.t: Genji said, "Of course.

units.source_text: 听到和琴这个名词，似乎觉得是乡村田舍的低级乐器。

en.t: When people hear the name wagon, they may imagine it to be a rustic, lowly instrument of the countryside.

units.source_text: 岂知御前管弦演奏时，首先宣召掌管和琴的书司女官。

en.t: But in musical performances before the sovereign, the first person summoned is the female official of the library office who is in charge of the wagon.

units.source_text: 外国如何，不得而知；在我日本国，以和琴为乐器之始祖。

en.t: I do not know how it is in foreign countries, but in our Japan the wagon is regarded as the ancestor of musical instruments.

units.source_text: 倘能向和琴名手中最高明的内大臣学习，自然特别容易学好。

en.t: If you could learn from the Minister of the Center, the finest of all wagon masters, you would naturally find it especially easy to improve.

units.source_text: 今后但逢适当机会，他也会到这里来。

en.t: From now on, whenever a suitable occasion arises, he too will come here.

units.source_text: 然而要他不惜此琴妙技，将秘曲尽行表演，却是困难之事。

en.t: Yet it would be difficult to make him freely display all the subtle skills of this instrument and perform every secret piece.

units.source_text: 不论何种技艺，凡精通此道之人，都不肯轻易传授其秘诀。

en.t: Whatever the art may be, those who have mastered it are never willing to pass on its secrets lightly.

units.source_text: 但你将来总有机会听到。”

en.t: But in time you will surely have a chance to hear him."

units.source_text: 说罢，便取过琴来，弹了一个片段，音节非常新颖而华美。

en.t: Having said this, he took up the instrument and played a short passage, whose notes were remarkably fresh and splendid.

units.source_text: 玉鬘听了，想象内大臣弹得一定比他更好，思亲之心越发深切了。

en.t: As Tamakazura listened, she imagined that the Minister of the Center must surely play even better than he did, and her longing for her father grew still deeper.

units.source_text: 为了和琴之事，也使她增添烦恼：不知哪一天能蒙父亲诚恳亲切地弹给我听？

en.t: The matter of the wagon added to her sorrow as well: she wondered when her father might kindly and warmly play it for her to hear.
